question.text: What is a 'collar' strategy in equity and currency markets?

answer.text: Long the underlying + buy an OTM put (downside protection) + sell an OTM call (finance the put premium) — it creates a range where profit and loss are both limited, often at zero or low net cost
A regulatory limit on maximum position sizes
Buying both a call and put at the same strike
A special order type that prevents execution outside a price range

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity collar: Long stock + Long OTM put + Short OTM call. The call premium received partly or fully offsets the put premium paid. Result: downside capped at put strike, upside capped at call strike. Zero-cost collar when premiums match. The Trap: A collar is not a position limit or an order type. Buying call + put at same strike is a straddle. The collar specifically involves the underlying position. Note: The collar template depends on the direction of underlying exposure. A long receivables/long-underlying position uses long put + short call. A USD payable/importer hedging USDINR appreciation uses a call-based collar — buy USDINR call (cap upside cost) and sell USDINR put (finance the call premium), per the Currency Derivatives workbook hedging guidance.
